clue.text: Cook cutting out a part of vegetable?

indicators.note: cutting out tells us to take the letter given by the next word out of the cooking word

parts.note: to steam food is one way to cook it

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to trim away part of a vegetable before cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting out' removes the A from STEAM. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a stalk is one part of a vegetable, though not of every one.
explanation.definitionFit: The stalk of a plant such as broccoli or asparagus is a part of the vegetable that is eaten.

clue.text: Fellow on phone gets prize-winning novelist

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a fellow is a man
TEL is the standard abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A man talking on the telephone turns out to be a celebrated author.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary Mantel won the Booker Prize twice, for Wolf Hall and Bring Up the Bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel is an English writer who won the Booker Prize twice, an example of an award-winning author.

clue.text: Bishop's office copies tape improperly

indicators.note: improperly says the letters of the two words before it are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bishop's office is caught duplicating tapes it should not.
explanation.definitionFit: The episcopate is the rank or term of office held by a bishop, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Like groups offering worldly goods

parts.note: as and like both mean in the same way as
sets are groups of things that belong together

explanation.surface: Similar bundles of things for sale on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's possessions, the property they own, are their assets in the accounting sense.

clue.text: A form of rule in Home Counties, supported by very old city

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the following pieces sit underneath
in says the first pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
the Raj was British rule in India

explanation.surface: A style of government in the English shires is propped up by an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's south-east, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Rubbish ultimately attracting rubbish

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Junk tends to draw more junk to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second gives ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for junk or dirt, a colloquial synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Shy, taking clothes off etc?

definitions.meaning: going to bed, which involves undressing and more, hence the etc and question mark

explanation.surface: A bashful person's habits when getting undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is going to bed for the night, which starts with undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is modest and shy; retiring also means going to bed, when clothes come off.

clue.text: Modern bits of language spreading gloominess

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters of the next word being scattered and laid out anew

explanation.surface: New slang is making everyone more miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Neologisms are newly coined words or expressions, recent additions to a language.

clue.text: Walk quietly past market, having turned back

indicators.note: past means the quiet letter goes beyond, after, the other piece
having turned back says the word for a market is read backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone strolls softly by a market then retraces their steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or a long way on foot, a near synonym.

clue.text: See zebra moving east in wind

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the first two words shift into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Watch a zebra walking eastward into the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze blowing in off the sea is a kind of light wind.

clue.text: Artist sits awkwardly being welcomed in West?

indicators.note: being welcomed in says the jumbled letters go inside the name of the film star

parts.note: Mae West was an American film star, so West hints at her first name

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of sits are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter perches uncomfortably while being received in the western part of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West?' looks like a direction; the question mark flags it as a surname, Mae West's.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leading figure of Fauvism, so an example of an artist.

clue.text: A new excitement when king emerges from earthy mound

indicators.note: emerges from says the king's letter comes out of the word for excitement

parts.note: a thrill is a burst of excitement
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A fresh thrill as a monarch climbs out of a heap of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants pile up soil and debris over their nest, making a small earth mound.

clue.text: One has darkness, no end, in native dwelling

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: no end says the last letter of the word for darkness is dropped

parts.note: gloom is darkness

explanation.surface: A person sits in endless darkness inside a traditional home.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow house built by Inuit peoples is a traditional dwelling of Arctic natives.

clue.text: Unimportant stuff this person's brought to the fore

indicators.note: brought to the fore says the speaker's piece goes in front

parts.note: this person is the speaker, so this person's is I am, shortened to I'm
material is stuff, matter

explanation.surface: Insignificant possessions belonging to the speaker are pushed into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaterial does not matter: it is irrelevant or of no consequence.

clue.text: Carol wrapping Ted maybe in protective covering

indicators.note: wrapping says the word for carol goes round the surname

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
Ted Heath was a British prime minister, so Ted is a clue to the surname

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol bundles up a man called Ted in something to keep him safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol and Ted read as names; Carol is a verb and Ted points to Edward Heath, UK prime minister 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathing is a layer that encases something, such as cable or timber, to shield it.

clue.text: Unfaithful love rat, suitor gets upset about

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the zero
gets upset says the letters of the two words are overturned into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A cheating suitor, a real rat, becomes upset in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitorous person betrays trust, so is disloyal or unfaithful.

clue.text: Fruit obtainable from San Marino garden

indicators.note: obtainable from says the letters can be got out of the following words when reworked

explanation.surface: A fruit that can be picked in a garden in San Marino.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin oranges are small, loose-skinned citrus fruits.

clue.text: Chap blocks road in that revolutionary conqueror's home region

indicators.note: in says the blocked road sits inside the turned word
revolutionary says the old word for that is turned round

parts.note: yon is an old word for that

indicators.note: blocks says the fellow sits in the middle of the road, obstructing it

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man barricades a road in the homeland of a revolutionary conqueror.
explanation.walkthrough: William the Conqueror was Duke of Normandy before invading England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror came from this region of northern France, where he was duke.

clue.text: Pause during session with one needing little time

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a term is a session of a school or court
the Roman numeral for one is I
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Taking a break in a school term because someone needs a bit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or stop for a while, so it means to pause.

clue.text: Worried rodent met snakes

indicators.note: snakes, as a verb, says the letters twist and wind into a new order

explanation.surface: A rat was frightened on encountering snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakes' reads as a plural noun; it is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormented means harassed or plagued, as a worry nags at someone.

clue.text: Champion fed up, having obtained goal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A winner who is sick of it all after scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as a noun but is the verb, to stand up for.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support or stand up for it, the same as to defend it.

clue.text: Groan maybe as recipient of holy letter

definitions.meaning: ... Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels, so Groan is a surname needing its first name
Saint Paul's Epistle to this early Christian is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A moan from someone who has received a letter from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Groan is the Gormenghast hero, and Paul wrote a New Testament letter to Titus.

clue.text: Volunteers landing on Caribbean country but not a Pacific island

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: but not says the following letter is removed from the country

parts.note: Haiti is a country in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Volunteer troops make a landing in the Caribbean rather than on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Minister embraces a device for generating energy

indicators.note: embraces says the clergyman's word holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: a rector is a parish minister in the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman hugs a machine that makes power.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the apparatus in a power station where energy is produced.

clue.text: Understanding the performance, he won't participate

indicators.note: won't participate says the pronoun takes no part, so its letters are removed

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A man declines to join in the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitive understanding of how to handle people without giving offence.

clue.text: There's little right in Dad being more distant

indicators.note: in says the short letter goes inside the parent's word

parts.note: dad is a familiar word for father
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: Dad is hardly ever right, and growing distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Farther is the comparative of far, meaning at a greater distance.

clue.text: Bit of money made by heartless competitor

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the competitor's word is removed

parts.note: a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: Cold-hearted opponents make some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is a currency unit of Iran, Oman and Yemen, so a piece of money.

clue.text: Bug one's caught? Supplement will limit cold

indicators.note: will limit says the extra's word encloses the cold letter, hemming it in

parts.note: an addition is a supplement, something added
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether you have caught a bug and suggests a supplement for your cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a virus; the question mark says it is an obsession one gets hooked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bitten by a bug means becoming obsessed or hooked, a dependence like addiction.

clue.text: Extremist contributing to awful tragedy

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fanatic played a part in a terrible disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, especially in politics, a synonym for a radical.
